bottleneck.description: Sole dominant global producer of separated NdPr oxide from the Bayan Obo deposit; controls ~90% of refined rare-earth magnet feedstock at the production-quota level, with no viable Western alternative at scale.

dependency.key_customers: NdFeB magnet makers (JL Mag, Ningbo Yunsheng, Zhongke Sanhuan, Proterial/Hitachi Metals); downstream EV motor, robotics, wind turbine, and defense supply chains
dependency.key_suppliers: Baogang Group (parent — Bayan Obo mining), separation chemical suppliers, Chinese state coordination on export quotas

editorial.notes: CNRE controls the Bayan Obo complex (world's largest light rare earth resource) and is the dominant single producer of separated NdPr oxide globally. China collectively refines ~90% of global rare earth magnet inputs and CNRE is the largest single operator — its production quotas materially move global NdPr prices within weeks. The 2024 and 2025 Chinese rare-earth export controls (October 2024 Annex IV additions; April/October 2025 expansions covering medium and heavy REEs) have escalated geopolitical bite from 'concentration risk' to 'active supply-chain weaponisation' — clearing the CRITICAL bar of 'no alternative exists today'. MP Materials (Mountain Pass), Lynas, and emerging Western processing capacity (Arafura, etc.) collectively run at <15% of CNRE's separation throughput and lack heavy-rare-earth processing capability outside Lynas's Kalgoorlie ramp. Consolidated key (was split as '600111' HIGH from Robotics batch + '600111 C1' CRITICAL from existing rated set; the existing CRITICAL was the right call given full context).
